reconcile_note: Escalated best-of-N (1 fast pass + 3 blind candidates + grep backstop). All four converge on the same root cause and impersonation-is-incidental finding. The one real fork — resilience via Laravel's ShouldRescue marker on the events (candidates 1,3) vs explicit try/catch in the two services (fast-pass, candidate 2) — was settled by the driver reading the pinned vendor (Laravel 12.57.0): Illuminate\Contracts\Broadcasting\ShouldRescue exists and BroadcastManager::queue() wraps a ShouldBroadcastNow dispatch in rescue() (report+swallow) per-dispatch iff the event implements it. ShouldRescue is preferred: framework-native, ~2 lines, covers all 8 call sites uniformly, per-dispatch so bulk loops complete, and reports failures. Two design questions remain genuinely human (failure UX; keep-vs-revert ShouldBroadcastNow) → gate BLOCKED.
synthesis: In Clarity Scout, assigning a kit user to a zone (map editor ManageZones::save()) can throw a server-side exception that Filament v5 renders as its generic 'Error while loading page' toast, and — worst case — silently rolls back the whole save so the assignment does not persist. Root cause: ManageZones::save() wraps the zone write, PostGIS geometry rebuild, zone_user pivot sync (ZoneAssignmentSyncer), and the real-time broadcast fan-out (ZoneBroadcaster) inside ONE DB::connection('platform')->transaction(). The two Scout events dispatched in that path — ZoneAssignmentsChanged and ZoneUpdated — implement ShouldBroadcastNow (switched from queued ShouldBroadcast in commit b51b21061 'Broadcast now', 2026-05-29), so the Pusher/Reverb HTTP push runs synchronously, in-request. Laravel's PusherBroadcaster only catches Pusher\ApiErrorException (rewrapped as BroadcastException); any other throwable (network/DNS/TLS/config), and even that BroadcastException, propagates uncaught out of the transaction closure → the whole save rolls back and the exception surfaces as the toast. It bites specifically on 'assigning a user' because ZoneBroadcaster::broadcastUpdated() is a no-op for a zone with zero assigned drivers, so the first assignment is the first synchronous broadcast the zone ever attempts. Desired outcome: a real-time broadcast delivery failure must never roll back or fail an otherwise-valid zone save/assignment (or any zone action); the DB write is durable and the push is best-effort + logged.

scope.summary: Make the two Scout zone broadcast events resilient by implementing Laravel 12's native Illuminate\Contracts\Broadcasting\ShouldRescue on both, so a synchronous ShouldBroadcastNow delivery failure is report()'d and swallowed by the framework instead of propagating — which (a) stops the DB transaction rollback in ManageZones::save() and (b) removes the misleading error toast from the 7 non-transactional zone actions, all from a single 2-line-per-file change at the choke point. Keep ShouldBroadcastNow (real-time immediacy) — reverting to queued ShouldBroadcast would still throw synchronously wherever QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync, so it is not a sufficient fix on its own. Add regression tests that exercise a REAL (non-Event::faked) broadcaster failure.

out_of_scope: Root-causing the specific production broadcast infra failure (Pusher/Reverb reachability, credentials, quota) for org 348942 — needs Nightwatch/Datadog + env access this read-only prep can't reach; the ShouldRescue fix removes the user-facing symptom regardless of the exact trigger. Deferred as a follow-up.

Restructuring ManageZones::save() to move the broadcast dispatch outside the DB transaction (defense-in-depth). Not required once ShouldRescue prevents the dispatch from ever throwing; adds churn for no additional guarantee.

Reverting ZoneAssignmentsChanged/ZoneUpdated to queued ShouldBroadcast — a deliberate architecture change (commit b51b21061) that trades real-time immediacy for isolation, and insufficient on its own (still throws synchronously under QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync). Flagged as an open question, not silently reverted.

questions.q: Failure UX: when a real-time broadcast fails, should the admin see NOTHING (silent + logged) or a soft warning toast?
questions.answer: Silent + logged. Save shows the normal 'Zone saved' success toast; broadcast failures are report()'d to error tracking (via Laravel's rescue()). Drivers still get the persisted DB notification on next refetch. No soft warning (Dalton confirmed pure ShouldRescue over the try/catch-warning variants, understanding ShouldRescue swallows the failure inside the framework so a warning isn't possible without extra plumbing).

questions.q: Resilience mechanism / architecture: ShouldRescue marker vs try/catch in services vs revert to queued ShouldBroadcast?
questions.answer: ShouldRescue on both events (ZoneAssignmentsChanged + ZoneUpdated), KEEPING ShouldBroadcastNow. Framework-native, ~2 lines per event, per-dispatch rescue so bulk loops complete, failures report()'d. Not try/catch (more surface), not revert-to-queued (still throws under QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync).

questions.q: Is admin impersonation causal to this bug?
questions.answer: No — incidental. ImpersonateController::impersonate() does a real Auth::loginUsingId(), so auth()->user()/org resolution is identical to a directly-logged-in org admin; ZonePolicy gates on ADMIN-role scoped to the org regardless of the admin_impersonator flag. The broadcast failure path never reads impersonation state. Impersonation is just how internal staff reach another org's Zones page.

questions.q: Does the error fire on selecting the user (live) or on Save?
questions.answer: On Save. The 'Assigned Kit Users' Select is ->live() but has NO afterStateUpdated hook (ManageZones.php:162-198) — selecting a user only re-renders Livewire state. The zone_user sync + broadcast happen exclusively in save() inside the DB transaction (ManageZones.php:296-311).

questions.q: Would a metadata-only edit (no roster change) on the same zone also fail?
questions.answer: Yes, if the zone already has ≥1 assigned driver — ZoneBroadcaster::broadcastUpdated() iterates every currently-assigned user regardless of whether the roster changed, so it attempts the same synchronous broadcast. Only a zone with zero assigned drivers and no roster change skips broadcasting entirely. The event-level ShouldRescue fix covers this case too.

notes: Verified in pinned vendor (Laravel 12.57.0): Illuminate\Contracts\Broadcasting\ShouldRescue exists; BroadcastManager::queue() (lines 180-189) dispatches ShouldBroadcastNow synchronously and wraps it in $this->rescue() (→ global rescue(), which report()s and swallows) ONLY when the event also implements ShouldRescue. This is the framework's purpose-built mechanism for exactly this bug and is per-dispatch (so bulk loops complete).

CI is structurally blind to this class: every Zone broadcast test uses Event::fake(), and .env.testing sets no BROADCAST_CONNECTION so it falls back to the 'log' driver (never throws). New tests must force a REAL throwing broadcaster, not Event::fake().

Only ManageZones::save() wraps the broadcast in a DB transaction (the data-loss case). The other 7 sites (delete, quick-edit, reassign ×3, bulk-delete, restore) already commit before dispatching, so a throw there is a misleading toast (and, for the two bulk loops, a mid-loop abort) — all fixed transitively by the event-level change.

Repo already has a best-effort side-effect convention (app/Services/Rdn/RdnMetricsPublisher.php catch(\Throwable)+report()+log) — cited as the try/catch alternative; ShouldRescue achieves the same report+swallow with less surface.
The events share the broadcastAs name 'zones.changed'; the Scout client refetches on it. ShouldRescue does not change the success-path payload/channel.
okf/concepts/scout-real-time-tracking.md documents the zone-broadcast flow but not this resiliency gap — a wiki update is worth proposing at handoff (not created per CLAUDE.md unless asked).

grounding.code_flow: ManageZones (Livewire) wire:submit=save → save() opens DB::connection('platform')->transaction() → Zone::fill/save + rebuildGeometryFromDefinition (PostGIS) → ZoneAssignmentSyncer::syncZoneUsers (zone_user sync/attach + ScoutNotifier DB rows + event(ZoneAssignmentsChanged) per added/removed user) → ZoneBroadcaster::broadcastUpdated (event(ZoneUpdated) per remaining assigned user) → both events ShouldBroadcastNow → BroadcastManager::queue() dispatchNow → PusherBroadcaster::broadcast() (real HTTP) → any throwable propagates uncaught out of the transaction closure → full rollback + rethrow → Livewire non-2xx → Filament default 'Error while loading page' toast. Fix: ShouldRescue on both events makes BroadcastManager wrap each dispatch in rescue() (report+swallow) so nothing propagates.

exhaustiveness.idiom: Dispatching a ShouldBroadcastNow event (synchronous in-request Pusher/Reverb broadcast) with no ShouldRescue marker and no surrounding try/catch; any throwable propagates uncaught into the caller, and if the caller is inside a DB transaction it rolls back an otherwise-valid write.

sites.reason: Broadcast inside DB transaction — the ticket's exact repro; a throw rolls back the entire save + assignment. Fixed transitively by the 2 event changes.
Delete committed before broadcastDeleted; a throw shows a false error toast. Fixed transitively.
All funnel into syncZoneUsers; bulk loop aborts on first failure. Fixed transitively (per-dispatch rescue lets the loop complete).
record->save committed before broadcastUpdatedTo; false error toast. Fixed transitively.
Delete/restore committed before broadcast; bulk-delete loop aborts on first failure. Fixed transitively.
ZoneAssignmentsChanged + ZoneUpdated are the ONLY broadcasting event classes in the app; no other domain broadcasts synchronously, so the fragile idiom is confined to these two events.

data_impact.mv_or_cdc_implications: None — pure PostgreSQL (platform schema) write path plus an outbound broadcast HTTP call. No ClickHouse tables, materialized views, or CDC/PeerDB pipelines touched.
